tasks.script_en: Hi, Anna, it's Rosa. Our team meeting isn't at nine today. The boss has a call then. It's at ten thirty, in room twelve. Oh, and please bring your laptop. See you there!
tasks.question_en: When is the team meeting today?
tasks.explanation_ru: Роза сначала говорит, что встреча не в девять (isn't at nine today): в это время у начальника звонок. Новое время — It's at ten thirty, то есть 10:30. Twelve — номер комнаты.

tasks.script_en:
Mia: Hi, Alex. I'm leaving work. Do we need anything from the store?
Alex: Yes, please. Milk, bread, and two apples. Oh, and eggs.
Mia: OK. Or do you want to eat out tonight?
Alex: No, let's cook at home. See you soon!
tasks.question_en: What is the phone call mainly about?
options: Buying food after work
Cooking dinner for friends
Going back to work
Eating out tonight
tasks.explanation_ru: Главное в звонке — покупки по дороге домой: Do we need anything from the store? Алекс называет список: milk, bread, two apples, eggs. Поесть вне дома он отказывается (No, let's cook at home), о гостях речи нет, а с работы собеседница как раз уходит (I'm leaving work).

tasks.script_en: Hi, it's Sara, your new roommate. Here's my morning. I take a shower at seven. Then I eat breakfast. At eight, I walk to the bus stop. I get coffee at work, not at home. Bye!
tasks.question_en: What does Sara do right after breakfast?
options: Takes a shower at seven
Walks to the bus stop
Makes coffee at home
Gets coffee at work
tasks.explanation_ru: Порядок: душ at seven → Then I eat breakfast → At eight, I walk to the bus stop. Сразу после завтрака Сара идёт на остановку. Душ — до завтрака, а кофе она пьёт на работе: at work, not at home.

tasks.script_en: Hi, Mark, it's Lisa. I'm at the office. I need my laptop for my trip, but the front door is locked, and it's dark inside. It's seven on Sunday morning. Do you have a key?
tasks.question_en: Why can't Lisa get in?
options: The office is closed on Sunday
There's no electricity in the building
The front door is broken
It's too late in the evening
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо это не сказано, но дверь заперта (the front door is locked), внутри темно, а сейчас seven on Sunday morning — в выходной офис закрыт. Дверь не сломана, а заперта; об электричестве ничего не сказано; и сейчас утро, а не вечер.

tasks.script_en:
Zoe: So, Leo, how's your new coffee?
Leo: Mmm, it smells great, and it's nice and hot. But it's too sweet for me.
Zoe: Oh no. Do you want my tea?
Leo: No, thanks. Next time I'll order it without sugar.
tasks.question_en: How does Leo feel about the coffee?
options: Likes the smell but not the sweet taste
Likes the sweet taste but not the smell
Likes the smell but thinks it's too hot
Likes that it's hot but not the smell
tasks.explanation_ru: Лео хвалит запах (it smells great) и то, что кофе горячий (nice and hot), а недоволен вкусом: it's too sweet for me. Поэтому в следующий раз он закажет его without sugar.

tasks.script_en:
Emma: Excuse me, how much is this blue T-shirt?
Sam: It's fifteen dollars. The white one is twelve.
Emma: OK, I like the blue one. Do you have it in medium?
Sam: Yes, here you go.
tasks.question_en: How much is the blue T-shirt?
options: Twelve dollars
Fifteen dollars
Fifty dollars
Sixteen dollars
tasks.explanation_ru: Продавец называет цену синей футболки: It's fifteen dollars. Twelve — цена белой, а fifteen легко спутать с fifty: в fifteen ударение падает на второй слог.

tasks.script_en:
Anna: Hi, Tom!
Tom: Hi, Mom! Are you free on Saturday?
Anna: Yes, I think so. Why?
Tom: It's Ben's birthday. We're having a small party at our place at two. Can you come?
Anna: Of course! I'll bring a cake.
tasks.question_en: What is the phone call mainly about?
options: Asking Mom to bring a birthday cake
Inviting Mom to a birthday party
Planning a party at Mom's place
Asking Mom about her Saturday plans
tasks.explanation_ru: Том звонит, чтобы позвать маму на день рождения Бена: We're having a small party... Can you come? Торт мама предлагает принести сама (I'll bring a cake), а праздник будет у Тома — at our place.

tasks.script_en: Hi, it's Kate. Let's meet at the train station tomorrow at ten. First, we'll visit the art museum. Then we'll have lunch in the park. After lunch, we can go shopping, OK? See you!
tasks.question_en: What will they do right after the museum?
options: Go shopping
Have lunch in the park
Go back to the station
Have coffee at home
tasks.explanation_ru: Порядок такой: встреча на вокзале → музей → Then we'll have lunch in the park → After lunch, we can go shopping. Сразу после музея — обед в парке, магазины потом.

tasks.script_en:
Jack: Good evening. A table for two, please.
Nina: Sure. Inside or by the window?
Jack: By the window, please. And can we see the menu?
Nina: Here you are. Today's soup is tomato.
tasks.question_en: Where are the two speakers?
options: On a train
In a restaurant
In a food store
At a friend's home
tasks.explanation_ru: Место прямо не названо, но A table for two, please, просьба показать menu и Today's soup is tomato — это ресторан. Место у окна бывает и в поезде, но столик на двоих и суп дня там не предлагают.

tasks.script_en: I love my new apartment. It's small, but the kitchen is big and bright. The only problem is the noise. The street is very busy at night. But I'm really happy here.
tasks.question_en: How does the speaker feel about the new apartment?
options: Happy, but the street is noisy
Unhappy, because it is too small
Happy, but the kitchen is too small
Unhappy, and wants to move
tasks.explanation_ru: Говорящий доволен: I love my new apartment и I'm really happy here. Минус один — шум: The only problem is the noise. Маленькая сама квартира, а кухня как раз big and bright; переезжать он не собирается.

tasks.script_en:
Lucy: Good morning, Oak Street Dental. This is Lucy.
Mike: Hi, this is Mike Brown. I have an appointment on Thursday at nine, but I can't come. Can I change it?
Lucy: Sure. We have Friday at eleven fifteen or Monday at four.
Mike: Friday, please. Eleven fifty, right?
Lucy: No, eleven fifteen.
Mike: OK, thanks!
tasks.question_en: When is Mike's new appointment?
options: Thursday at 9:00
Friday at 11:15
Friday at 11:50
Monday at 4:00
tasks.explanation_ru: Майк переносит приём с четверга (Thursday at nine). Ему предлагают Friday at eleven fifteen or Monday at four, он выбирает пятницу, а на его переспрос Eleven fifty, right? отвечают: No, eleven fifteen — 11:15.

tasks.script_en: Hi, team, it's Helen. Just a quick message. I usually come into the office on Tuesdays, but today I'm working from home. A plumber's coming to fix my kitchen sink, sometime between ten and two. Don't worry, I'll join all our meetings online. See you on the screen!
tasks.question_en: What is Helen mainly telling the team?
options: She's sick today and will miss all the meetings
She's at home today but joining the meetings
A plumber is coming to fix the sink in the office
All today's meetings are moving online
tasks.explanation_ru: Главное: сегодня Хелен работает из дома (today I'm working from home), но на все встречи подключится: I'll join all our meetings online. Сантехник придёт к ней домой чинить раковину (my kitchen sink), а онлайн встречи только для неё, а не для всей команды. О болезни речи нет.

tasks.script_en:
Omar: Hi, Julia. Can I deploy the new version now?
Julia: Not yet, Omar. First, check that all the tests are green.
Omar: They're green.
Julia: Good. Then ask Maria to review your change. When she approves it, you can deploy.
Omar: And after that?
Julia: Tell the support team in the chat.
tasks.question_en: What must happen right before Omar deploys the new version?
options: He checks that the tests are green
He asks Maria to review the change
Maria approves his change
He tells the support team
tasks.explanation_ru: Порядок: tests are green → ask Maria to review your change → When she approves it, you can deploy → сообщить поддержке. Непосредственно перед выкладкой — одобрение Марии; просьба о ревью идёт раньше, а сообщение поддержке — уже после (And after that?).

tasks.script_en:
Sofia: Hi, Ken. Is Leo at lunch? His chair's empty.
Ken: No, he sent me a photo this morning. Look, he's at the airport with a big suitcase!
Sofia: Oh! When's he back in the office?
Ken: Next Monday. And he looks very happy in the photo.
tasks.question_en: Why isn't Leo at his desk?
options: He's in a long meeting
He's out at lunch
He's sick at home
He's away on a trip
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо это не сказано, но Лео прислал фото: he's at the airport with a big suitcase, — и вернётся только next Monday: он в поездке. Про обед Кен отвечает No, о встрече речи нет, а больным Лео не выглядит: he looks very happy.

tasks.script_en: So, did you get the new update for the bank app? I think it's much better. It looks cleaner, and the search is really fast now. The only problem is the settings. I can't find them anywhere! But overall, I like it a lot more than the old version.
tasks.question_en: What does the speaker think of the update?
options: Likes the new look, but finds the search slower
Likes the fast search, but misses the old look
Likes the look and search, but not the settings
Likes the settings, but finds the look too plain
tasks.explanation_ru: Говорящей нравится внешний вид (It looks cleaner) и быстрый поиск (the search is really fast now), а минус один — настройки: I can't find them anywhere! В целом новая версия ей нравится больше старой: I like it a lot more than the old version.

tasks.script_en: Attention, please. Passengers on flight three twenty to Denver, your flight is delayed by forty minutes because of snow. The new departure time is five fifty. Please stay near gate twelve. We're sorry for the delay, and thank you for your patience.
tasks.question_en: What is the new departure time?
tasks.explanation_ru: Новое время названо прямо: The new departure time is five fifty — 5:50. Three twenty — номер рейса, forty minutes — длительность задержки, а fifty легко спутать с fifteen.

tasks.script_en:
Ella: Hi, I'd like something for a sore throat, please.
Ron: Sure. Do you have a fever too?
Ella: No, but I've had a bad cough since Monday.
Ron: OK, try this syrup twice a day. If you don't feel better in three days, see a doctor.
tasks.question_en: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Making an appointment with a doctor
Getting medicine for a throat and cough
Buying medicine to bring down a fever
Asking when the pharmacy opens on Monday
tasks.explanation_ru: Покупательница просит something for a sore throat, рассказывает про кашель, и ей советуют сироп twice a day. К врачу идти нужно, только если через три дня не станет лучше; температуры у неё нет (No), а Monday — день, когда начался кашель.

tasks.script_en:
Paul: Excuse me, how do I get to the post office?
Maya: Go straight to the bank, then turn left. Walk past the park, and it's on your right, next to a small café.
Paul: So, left at the bank, then past the park?
Maya: That's right. It's about five minutes.
tasks.question_en: What will the man walk past right after he turns left?
options: The bank
The park
A small café
The post office
tasks.explanation_ru: Маршрут: straight to the bank → turn left → Walk past the park → почта справа, рядом с кафе. После поворота мужчина проходит мимо парка; банк остаётся до поворота, а кафе стоит уже у самой почты.

tasks.script_en: Hi, it's Carol from next door. I found a little brown dog in my backyard this morning. It has a red collar with your phone number on it. Don't worry, it's fine, and it's eating now. Please call me when you get home.
tasks.question_en: What has probably happened?
options: The listener's dog got out of the house
Carol has lost her own dog
The dog got hurt in Carol's backyard
Carol wants to give the listener a dog
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо это не сказано, но на ошейнике номер телефона слушателя (your phone number), а нашлась собака у соседки — значит, это собака слушателя и она сбежала из дома. С ней всё в порядке (it's fine), а свою собаку Кэрол не теряла.

tasks.script_en:
Kim: So, Dan, how was the movie last night? Everybody's talking about it.
Dan: Well, the actors were great, but it was way too long. Almost three hours!
Kim: Would you see it again?
Dan: Hmm, maybe at home, but not at the movie theater.
tasks.question_en: What does Dan think of the movie?
options: He loved it and wants to see it again soon
He liked the actors but found it too long
He didn't like the actors but liked the story
He thought it was boring from start to end
tasks.explanation_ru: Дэн хвалит актёров (the actors were great), но жалуется на длину: way too long. Almost three hours! Пересмотреть он готов разве что дома (maybe at home), а не в кинотеатре.

tasks.script_en:
Nadia: Hi, Tariq. Quick question about the client report. Is it still due Thursday afternoon?
Tariq: Well, that was the plan. But finance can't send their numbers until Thursday evening.
Nadia: Oh no. So what did you tell the client?
Tariq: I called them this morning. They're OK with Friday, as long as it's before noon.
Nadia: Great, that gives us a bit more time. I'll tell the team.
tasks.question_en: When is the report due now?
options: Thursday afternoon
Thursday evening
Friday before noon
Friday afternoon
tasks.explanation_ru: Старый срок — Thursday afternoon, но финансисты пришлют цифры только Thursday evening, поэтому Тарик договорился с клиентом: They're OK with Friday, as long as it's before noon — пятница до полудня.

tasks.script_en: Hi, this is Carmen, the building manager. So, just a heads-up for everyone on the third floor. On Wednesday, the plumbers are replacing the old pipes, so there won't be any water from nine to about three. The elevator will work as usual, don't worry. I mean, it's only one day, but please fill a few bottles on Tuesday night. Thanks, and sorry for the trouble.
tasks.question_en: What is the message mainly about?
options: A day without water because of pipe work
Repairs to the elevator on the third floor
A new rule about saving water at night
Moving residents to another floor on Wednesday
tasks.explanation_ru: Главное: в среду меняют трубы, поэтому there won't be any water from nine to about three. Лифт работает as usual, а бутылки советуют наполнить заранее — это подготовка к одному дню без воды, а не новое правило экономии.

tasks.script_en: Hey, it's Priya. So, the call with the customer went fine, I think. They want two changes: a bigger export button and, um, a dark mode. Could you write those down and send the notes to the team today? Once everyone's checked them, go ahead and create the tickets. But please don't estimate anything yet. We'll do that together at tomorrow's planning meeting. Thanks!
tasks.question_en: What should the listener do after the team checks the notes?
options: Create the tickets
Estimate the work
Call the customer again
Send the notes to the team
tasks.explanation_ru: Порядок: записать две правки → отправить заметки команде → Once everyone's checked them, go ahead and create the tickets → оценка на завтрашнем planning meeting. Сразу после проверки — завести тикеты, а оценивать пока нельзя: don't estimate anything yet.

tasks.script_en:
Lena: So, Hugo, what did you think of Sam?
Hugo: Well, at first I wasn't sure. He hardly said a word for the first ten minutes.
Lena: Yeah. But once we got to real production problems, he just kept going.
Hugo: Right, lots of detail. And he asked good questions about monitoring and support duty.
Lena: He even made a joke at the end, you know, about our old dashboards.
tasks.question_en: What can we guess about Sam?
options: He has little experience with production systems
He became more comfortable as the interview went on
He's more interested in support than in development
He didn't take the interview very seriously
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо это не сказано, но сначала Сэм hardly said a word, потом на теме production problems he just kept going, задавал вопросы и даже пошутил в конце — он освоился. Опыт с production у него как раз виден, о поддержке он лишь спрашивал, а шутка в конце — знак того, что он расслабился, а не несерьёзности.

tasks.script_en:
Daniel: Hey, Aisha, how's that pottery class going?
Aisha: Oh, I love it. The teacher's amazing, and Tuesday evening's perfect for me.
Daniel: Isn't it expensive, though?
Aisha: Well, it's not cheap, but it's worth it. The only thing is, there are twenty people in the group, so the teacher hardly ever gets to me. You know, I wait ages just to ask one question. I'm going to ask about a smaller group next month.
tasks.question_en: How does Aisha feel about the pottery class?
options: Likes the teacher, but not the size of the group
Likes the group, but not the teacher
Likes the teacher, but thinks it costs too much
Likes the lessons, but not the Tuesday evening time
tasks.explanation_ru: Айша хвалит преподавателя (The teacher's amazing) и время (Tuesday evening's perfect), о цене говорит it's worth it, а недовольна одним: there are twenty people in the group, so the teacher hardly ever gets to me. Поэтому она спросит про группу поменьше.

tasks.script_en:
Olivia: Hi, I have a reservation under Martinez, for two nights.
Jake: Let me check. Yes, here it is. You're in room four oh six, on the fourth floor.
Olivia: Great. And what time is breakfast?
Jake: On weekdays, it's from six thirty to ten, but on weekends it starts at seven.
Olivia: And tomorrow's Saturday, right?
Jake: That's right.
tasks.question_en: What time does breakfast start tomorrow?
tasks.explanation_ru: Завтра суббота (tomorrow's Saturday), а on weekends it starts at seven — в 7:00. С 6:30 завтрак начинается только по будням, а ten — время, когда он заканчивается.

tasks.script_en: Good morning, this is City Radio with your local news. Starting next month, the city's bike-sharing program is expanding to the east side, with thirty new stations. Rides under thirty minutes will stay free for anyone with a city card, and visitors will be able to pay by phone. The mayor says the goal is to cut traffic downtown, especially during rush hour.
tasks.question_en: What is the news story mainly about?
options: Free bus rides for people with a city card
The bike-sharing program growing to a new area
A new app that lets visitors pay by phone
The mayor's plan to close downtown to cars
tasks.explanation_ru: Главная новость — расширение велопроката: the city's bike-sharing program is expanding to the east side, with thirty new stations. Бесплатные поездки по city card и оплата по телефону — детали, а закрывать центр для машин никто не собирается: мэр хочет лишь cut traffic.

tasks.script_en:
Sophie: Dad, I'm making your pancakes, but I forgot the order.
Mike: OK, Sophie. Mix the flour, sugar, and salt first. Then add the milk and eggs.
Sophie: And the butter? Do I just put it in the pan?
Mike: No, melt it and add it to the batter at the end. Then let it rest for ten minutes before you cook anything.
Sophie: Got it. Rest, then cook.
Mike: Exactly.
tasks.question_en: What should Sophie do right after adding the milk and eggs?
options: Put butter in the pan
Add the melted butter
Let the batter rest
Start cooking the pancakes
tasks.explanation_ru: Порядок: flour, sugar, salt → milk and eggs → растопленное масло at the end → rest for ten minutes → жарить. Масло не кладут на сковороду (No, melt it), а отдыхать тесто оставляют уже после масла.

tasks.script_en:
Megan: Hey, Tyler, are you still coming to the game tonight?
Tyler: I'd love to, Megan, but have you looked outside?
Megan: Oh. Yeah, it's really coming down. Do you think they'll play?
Tyler: Last time it was like this, they waited two hours and then sent everyone home. I'll watch it on TV, if they play at all.
Megan: Fair enough. I'm still going. I've got a good umbrella.
tasks.question_en: What does Tyler expect to happen tonight?
options: The game will be delayed or canceled
The game will start two hours early
Megan will decide to stay at home
The game won't be shown on TV
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо Тайлер этого не говорит, но вспоминает, что в прошлый раз в такую погоду they waited two hours and then sent everyone home, и добавляет if they play at all — он ждёт задержки или отмены. Матч он собирается смотреть по телевизору, а Меган всё равно пойдёт: I'm still going.

tasks.script_en: I've been going to the new gym on Pine Street for a month now. The equipment's brand-new, and the staff are really friendly. But honestly, for eighty dollars a month, I expected longer hours. It closes at nine, which is too early for me. I'll probably stay until my contract ends, and then I'll look for something cheaper.
tasks.question_en: How does the speaker feel about the gym?
options: Happy with it and planning to stay for years
Likes it but feels it isn't worth the price
Dislikes the staff but likes the equipment
Likes the hours but not the equipment
tasks.explanation_ru: Оборудование и персонал говорящий хвалит (brand-new, really friendly), но за eighty dollars a month ждал более долгих часов работы и после окончания контракта поищет something cheaper — цена кажется ему завышенной.

tasks.script_en:
Ines: OK, Ravi, the cloud bill. It went up, what, twenty percent last quarter?
Ravi: Eighteen, actually. Mostly because the analytics cluster was running all night, every night.
Ines: And if we turn it off outside business hours?
Ravi: That should save us roughly twelve thousand dollars a month. Maybe a bit less in the first month, since we need to move a couple of night jobs.
Ines: And the storage change you mentioned?
Ravi: Another three thousand, give or take. So fifteen in total, once both are done.
tasks.question_en: How much should the storage change save each month?
options: About three thousand dollars
About twelve thousand dollars
About fifteen thousand dollars
About eighteen thousand dollars
tasks.explanation_ru: Twelve thousand — экономия от выключения кластера на ночь, а storage change даёт Another three thousand, give or take. Fifteen — общая сумма обеих мер, а eighteen — рост счёта в процентах (Eighteen, actually).

tasks.script_en:
Kara: So, Luis, did you talk to the contractor?
Luis: Yeah. He says redoing the whole kitchen at once would take about five weeks. Well, six, realistically. And we'd have no kitchen at all the whole time.
Kara: Six weeks of takeout? With two kids? No way.
Luis: That's what I thought. So here's the idea: we start with the cabinets and the sink in May, live with it for a bit, and, if the budget still looks OK, we do the floor and the appliances in the fall.
Kara: Slower, but at least we can still cook. OK, let's do that.
tasks.question_en: What does the couple decide?
options: To redo the whole kitchen at once and eat out for six weeks
To renovate in stages, starting with the cabinets and sink
To do only the cabinets and sink and stop there
To wait until the fall and then redo everything at once
tasks.explanation_ru: Переделать кухню сразу — это шесть недель без кухни (Well, six, realistically), и на это пара не согласна: Six weeks of takeout? No way. Решают идти по частям: we start with the cabinets and the sink in May, а пол и технику сделают in the fall, если позволит бюджет. Остановиться на шкафах никто не предлагает.

tasks.script_en:
Kenji: So, Diana, I'm off from Friday. Well, Thursday afternoon, really. What do you need from me before I go?
Diana: Three things, Kenji. First, update the incident guide. It's, well, a bit out of date since the last outage.
Kenji: Fair. And the payment issue?
Diana: Right, walk Nina through it. It's still open, so she'll need the full story. She takes over your support rotation on Monday.
Kenji: Should I just set up the handover call now?
Diana: Not yet. She can't see the dashboard, so ask security to give her access first. Then book the call. Otherwise, you know, you'll be showing her screens she can't open.
tasks.question_en: According to Diana, what has to happen right before Kenji books the handover call?
options: The payment issue must be closed
Nina must get access to the dashboard
Nina must take over the support rotation
Kenji must walk Nina through the payment issue
tasks.explanation_ru: Диана прямо задаёт порядок: ask security to give her access first. Then book the call — иначе Кенджи будет показывать Нине экраны, которые она не может открыть. Дежурство Нина примет только on Monday, платёжная проблема всё ещё открыта (It's still open), а разобрать её с Ниной Кенджи и должен на этом созвоне.

tasks.script_en: OK, quick update on Friday's launch. Marketing's already got the announcement ready, and the feature passed all its functional tests on Tuesday. Well, technically Wednesday morning, after the last fix went in. So on paper, everything's green. Still, our team lead's asked everyone to keep Friday evening free, and not to plan any trips that weekend. She's also booked an extra rollback rehearsal for Thursday, and she wants support to have instructions for the old version ready, just in case. So, you know, I wouldn't book anything yet.
tasks.question_en: What is the team lead probably concerned about?
options: Marketing announcing the feature too early
Problems in production after the launch
The feature failing its functional tests
The announcement not being ready in time
tasks.explanation_ru: Функциональные тесты пройдены и анонс готов, но тимлид просит держать свободными вечер пятницы и выходные, назначает extra rollback rehearsal и просит для поддержки инструкции к старой версии just in case — она опасается проблем в эксплуатации после запуска. О спешке маркетинга в записи ничего нет.

tasks.script_en: So, the solar panel guy came by yesterday. And honestly, the presentation was great: a slick video, pictures of our own roof, the works. I can see why the neighbors signed up. But every time I asked something difficult, like what happens if a panel breaks, he'd say, oh, the next model fixes that. The next model! And it's a twenty-year lease. No, sorry, twenty-five. I'm not saying no, exactly. But I'm not signing anything until I've talked to a few people who've actually had these panels for a while.
tasks.question_en: How does the speaker feel about the offer?
options: Impressed by the presentation, but doubtful about the promises
Impressed by the promises, but not by the presentation
Worried about the long lease, but ready to wait for the next model
Pleased with the long lease, but not with the video
tasks.explanation_ru: Презентацию говорящая хвалит (the presentation was great) и понимает соседей, но на каждый трудный вопрос звучало the next model fixes that, а аренда — на двадцать пять лет. Поэтому она ничего не подпишет, пока не поговорит с теми, у кого такие панели уже стоят. Ждать следующей модели она не собирается.

tasks.script_en:
Rachel: Hi, is this Victor? I'm calling about the two-bedroom on Maple Avenue. Is it still available?
Victor: It is. Rent's eighteen hundred a month, and that includes water and trash, but not electricity.
Rachel: OK. And what about the deposit?
Victor: It's one month's rent, so eighteen hundred. Oh, wait, sorry, for this unit it's actually fifteen hundred, since it hasn't been renovated yet.
Rachel: Got it. And pets? I've got a cat.
Victor: Cats are fine, but there's a fifty-dollar monthly pet fee.
tasks.question_en: How much is the deposit for this apartment?
tasks.explanation_ru: Сначала Виктор называет залог в размере месячной аренды (eighteen hundred), но тут же поправляется: for this unit it's actually fifteen hundred — $1,500. $1,800 — сама аренда, а $50 — ежемесячная плата за питомца.

tasks.script_en: Welcome back to Healthy Habits. So, today's question comes from a listener who, um, can't fall asleep before two in the morning. Now, most people blame their phones, and, well, screens do play a part. But the research we looked at, or most of it anyway, points somewhere else: to irregular schedules. If you go to bed at eleven on weekdays and at two or three on weekends, your body never really knows when night is. So before you buy another sleep app, try getting up at the same time every day, even on Sundays.
tasks.question_en: What is the host's main point?
options: Phones are the main reason people can't fall asleep
An irregular schedule matters more than screens
A good sleep app can fix an irregular schedule
Everyone should go to bed at eleven every night
tasks.explanation_ru: Ведущий признаёт, что screens do play a part, но главным называет другое: the research... points somewhere else: to irregular schedules — и советует вставать в одно и то же время каждый день. Покупать приложение он как раз не советует, а eleven — лишь пример будничного отбоя.

tasks.script_en:
Hannah: Hi, my suitcase didn't come out on the belt. I just flew in from Atlanta.
Oscar: Sorry about that. Can I see your baggage tag? Thanks, Hannah. OK, it looks like it's still in Atlanta. It'll be on the next flight, which lands at, uh, nine tonight. No, nine fifteen.
Hannah: So do I have to come back and pick it up?
Oscar: No. Once it lands, we'll scan it here, and then a courier will take it to your hotel, probably before midnight. Just fill out this form with your address before you leave.
Hannah: Great, thanks so much.
tasks.question_en: What will happen right after the suitcase is scanned?
options: Hannah will pick it up at the airport
A courier will take it to her hotel
It will be put on the next flight
Hannah will fill out a form
tasks.explanation_ru: Порядок: чемодан прилетит следующим рейсом (в 21:15) → we'll scan it here → and then a courier will take it to your hotel. Форму Ханна заполняет сейчас, до ухода из аэропорта, а возвращаться за багажом ей не нужно.

tasks.script_en:
Laura: So, how was Jamie's first swim meet?
Chris: Well, he came in last in both races. Actually, no, second to last in the relay.
Laura: Oh no. Was he upset?
Chris: That's the funny thing. He talked about it the whole way home: the starting blocks, the big timing boards, the older kids' dives. Then he asked if we could go to the pool on Saturday so he could practice his turns.
Laura: Sounds like you'll be spending a lot of weekends at the pool.
tasks.question_en: What can be inferred about Jamie?
options: He wants to quit swimming after losing
He's excited about swimming despite losing
He won one of his two races
He only enjoyed watching the older kids
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо это не сказано, но после проигрыша Джейми всю дорогу говорил о соревнованиях (talked about it the whole way home) и сам попросился в субботу в бассейн, чтобы practice his turns, — плавание его увлекло. Он ничего не выиграл: last и second to last.

tasks.script_en: So I finally called customer service about the broken blender. And I'll give them this: the woman I spoke to was lovely, really apologetic. But it took forty, no, closer to fifty minutes on hold just to reach her, and then she told me I'd have to mail it back at my own cost. For a blender that's two weeks old! I mean, I'll probably get my money back eventually, but I'm not buying anything from that company again.
tasks.question_en: How does the speaker feel about the company?
options: Satisfied, because the agent was so helpful
Frustrated, even though the agent was kind
Angry with the agent, but happy with the company
Worried that the money won't be refunded
tasks.explanation_ru: Сотрудницу говорящий хвалит (lovely, really apologetic), но почти пятьдесят минут ожидания и пересылка за свой счёт его злят, и вывод такой: I'm not buying anything from that company again. Деньги он, скорее всего, вернёт — probably get my money back eventually.

tasks.script_en:
Owen: So, the shorter signup form. Nine percent more registrations. I'd call that a win, Maya.
Maya: I'd love to, Owen, but look closer. Almost all of that came from mobile. Desktop didn't move at all.
Owen: Fine, but mobile's where most of our traffic is anyway.
Maya: True. Here's what bothers me, though. Email verification actually went down. Two percent. Well, one point eight, if you want to be precise.
Owen: That could just be noise.
Maya: Could be. But if people sign up and never verify, those nine percent aren't real users, are they? I'd keep the form and test a clearer verification screen before we call it a success.
tasks.question_en: Which metric got worse during the experiment?
options: Mobile registrations
Desktop conversion
Email verification
Overall registrations
tasks.explanation_ru: Регистраций стало на девять процентов больше, почти целиком за счёт mobile, desktop не изменился (Desktop didn't move at all), а вот подтверждение почты снизилось: Email verification actually went down — на 1,8 %. Поэтому Майя не спешит объявлять эксперимент успешным.

tasks.script_en:
Ethan: I've been thinking, Leah. With the new job, a second car would make life so much easier. No more juggling who drops the kids off.
Leah: I get it, Ethan, I do. But think about what comes with it: insurance, parking, another round of repairs, and the thing would sit outside the office all day.
Ethan: So you're saying no.
Leah: I'm saying not yet. Let's try the car-sharing app for, say, three months. Well, two might be enough. We keep track of how often we actually end up needing two cars at once. If it's every other day, fine, we buy one. If it's twice a month, we've saved ourselves a fortune.
tasks.question_en: What is Leah proposing?
options: Buying a second car now to make the school run easier
Buying a second car in a few months, whatever happens
Using car sharing for good instead of buying a car
Waiting to see how often they really need two cars
tasks.explanation_ru: Лия не отказывает (I'm saying not yet): она предлагает пару месяцев пользоваться каршерингом и считать, how often we actually end up needing two cars at once, — от этого и зависит покупка. Купить машину сразу хочет Итан, а отказаться от неё навсегда или купить её в любом случае никто не предлагает.

tasks.script_en:
Felix: Irene, sorry, it's three in the morning, but the checkout error alert just fired. Should I page the database team?
Irene: Hang on, Felix. First, make sure it's real. Is it customers, or is it the monitoring acting up again?
Felix: It's real. Support's already got, um, a dozen tickets. Fifteen now.
Irene: OK. Then you're the incident lead. Open the shared timeline, and then page the database team.
Felix: And management? Shouldn't they know?
Irene: Not until you've posted a first estimate of the impact. They'll only ask for numbers. The one exception: if anything looks like a security or legal issue, a data leak, say, you escalate straight away.
tasks.question_en: Normally, what must happen before management is told?
options: Security or legal approves the escalation
Felix posts a first impact estimate
The database team fixes the problem
The monitoring fault is repaired
tasks.explanation_ru: Ирина прямо ставит условие: Not until you've posted a first estimate of the impact. Security и legal — не согласование, а повод эскалировать сразу (straight away); чинить проблему до сообщения руководству не нужно, а сбоя мониторинга нет — It's real.

tasks.script_en:
Hana: Theo, have you been to Rosie's lately? Something feels off.
Theo: I was there on Saturday, actually. Half the pastry case was empty, and when I asked for the lemon cake, Rosie said she'd stopped ordering it. Not worth it anymore, apparently.
Hana: Huh. And she's giving out free coffee cards, but they're only good until the end of the month.
Theo: Oh, and one of the regulars told me she'd asked him if he knew anyone who wanted a good espresso machine. Cheap.
Hana: Plus there's no summer menu yet. She always puts it up in May, doesn't she?
Theo: Every year. I don't like where this is going.
tasks.question_en: What do the speakers suspect about the café?
options: Rosie is getting ready to close the café
Rosie is replacing her old espresso machine
Rosie is about to launch a new summer menu
Rosie has started baking her own cakes
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо никто этого не говорит, но Рози перестала заказывать выпечку (Not worth it anymore), бесплатные карты действуют only until the end of the month, она дёшево продаёт espresso machine и впервые не вывесила летнее меню — похоже, кафе закрывается. Машину она продаёт, а не меняет на новую, а о своей выпечке речи нет.

tasks.script_en: Can I just jump in here? I actually like the idea behind this. Getting people in the same room on purpose, not by accident, and two office days would really help the new hires. I mean, I started during lockdown, and it took me a year to learn who does what. What worries me is the one-size-fits-all part. Everyone, whatever their role, wherever they live, however their team's doing. We've got people three hours away. Well, two and a half, but still. If the policy had clear exceptions and, say, a review after three months, I'd be out there selling it for you.
tasks.question_en: Which description best matches the speaker's position?
options: Supports the rule, but wants more office days
Supports the goal, but objects to one rule for everyone
Supports the goal, but wants the rule for new hires only
Accepts the rule, but doubts it will help new hires
tasks.explanation_ru: Цель — собирать людей on purpose — говорящий поддерживает и считает, что два офисных дня помогут новичкам, но его беспокоит the one-size-fits-all part: одно правило для всех, whatever their role, wherever they live. С исключениями и пересмотром через три месяца он бы политику поддержал. Новичков он приводит как пример пользы, а не как единственную группу для правила.

tasks.script_en:
Grace: Martin, your first novel came out when you were in your fifties, so people tend to assume it took you decades to write.
Martin: Ha, they do. The truth is, I carried the idea around for about twenty years, but the actual writing took just under three. No, let me be honest, closer to four, if you count the rewrite my editor insisted on.
Grace: The rewrite being the new ending?
Martin: Right. In the original, the brother survives. My editor said, you know, the book had earned something darker, and she was right, annoyingly.
Grace: And the sequel?
Martin: Half-drafted. Don't hold your breath.
tasks.question_en: Including the rewrite, how long did the actual writing take?
options: Just under three years
Close to four years
About twenty years
Several decades
tasks.explanation_ru: Мартин сначала говорит just under three, но сразу поправляется: closer to four, if you count the rewrite. Twenty years он носил идею в голове, а decades — предположение публики, которое он опровергает.

tasks.script_en: In a vote late last night, the city council approved a plan that will, in effect, end single-family-only zoning across most of the city. Supporters argue that allowing duplexes and small apartment buildings on ordinary residential lots is the fastest way to bring rents down, or, well, at least to slow their rise. Opponents, many of them longtime homeowners, say the change was rushed and will put pressure on parking and schools. The plan doesn't take effect until January, and the council has promised to review its impact on traffic after the first year. Meanwhile, a petition to put the decision to a public vote is already circulating.
tasks.question_en: What is the report mainly about?
options: A new city rule that caps rents in apartment buildings
A council vote allowing more housing on residential lots
A homeowners' petition against new schools and parking
A study of how the new zoning has affected traffic
tasks.explanation_ru: Главное — решение совета: approved a plan that will... end single-family-only zoning, то есть на обычных участках разрешат дуплексы и небольшие дома. Снижение аренды — лишь надежда сторонников, петиция пока только собирает подписи, а влияние на трафик обещали изучить через год.

tasks.script_en:
Nora: So the train strike's confirmed for Tuesday. What does that do to our plan?
Adam: Well, we can't get to the coast on Tuesday, so let's flip it. We'll do the wine country first and pick up the rental car on Monday afternoon instead of Wednesday.
Nora: And drop it off where?
Adam: Back in the city, Wednesday night. Then Thursday morning we take the train to the coast, assuming the strike's over by then.
Nora: And if it isn't?
Adam: Then we just keep the car an extra day and drive. Oh, and first thing tomorrow we need to move the coast hotel from Tuesday to Thursday, before the prices jump.
tasks.question_en: Under the new plan, what will they do right after returning the car?
options: Drive out to the wine country
Take the train to the coast
Keep the car for an extra day
Move the coast hotel booking
tasks.explanation_ru: Новый порядок: в понедельник взять машину → винодельческий край → вернуть её в городе в среду вечером → Then Thursday morning we take the train to the coast. Лишний день с машиной — лишь запасной вариант, если забастовка не кончится, а отель переносят first thing tomorrow, ещё до поездки.

tasks.script_en: Hey, it's me. So I talked to Dad this afternoon. He says he's fine, and, you know, he probably is, mostly. But he asked me twice, maybe three times, what day it was, and when I mentioned his doctor's appointment, he said he'd never heard of it, even though he's the one who booked it. The fridge was nearly empty, too, which isn't like him at all. I don't want to make a big deal out of it, but maybe we should talk this weekend about, well, how often one of us drops by. Anyway, call me back when you can.
tasks.question_en: What is the caller most likely worried about?
options: Dad has stopped taking his medicine
Dad is struggling to manage on his own
Dad has argued with his doctor
Dad can no longer afford groceries
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо об этом не сказано, но отец несколько раз спрашивает, какой сегодня день, не помнит о приёме, который сам записал, а холодильник почти пустой (which isn't like him). Поэтому звонящий предлагает обсудить, how often one of us drops by, — отцу, похоже, уже трудно справляться одному. О лекарствах, ссоре с врачом или деньгах речи нет.

tasks.script_en:
Ruth: So, Leon, what did you make of it? You were very quiet at intermission.
Leon: I was trying to work out whether I liked it. The staging was extraordinary: that revolving set, the lighting in the second act.
Ruth: But?
Leon: But I never once cared what happened to anyone. It's as if the director was so pleased with the machinery that the actors became, well, furniture. Technically brilliant, emotionally, I'd say hollow. No, that's harsh. Cold.
Ruth: I'd have said the same about the first half, honestly, but the ending really got me.
Leon: See, Ruth, by then I was checking my watch.
tasks.question_en: What is Leon's opinion of the play?
options: He admired the staging but found it emotionally cold
He was bored in the first half but loved the ending
He disliked the set but thought the acting was strong
He found it moving but too long and too technical
tasks.explanation_ru: Постановку Леон хвалит (The staging was extraordinary), но ему ни разу не было дела до героев: I never once cared what happened to anyone, — и смягчает hollow до Cold. Финал понравился Рут, а Леон к тому времени смотрел на часы.

tasks.script_en:
Claire: Thanks. Claire Dawson here. Howard, your headline forecast is seven percent growth this year. How much of that hinges on the enterprise deal?
Howard: Fair question. The seven percent assumes that contract closes in September, and that we recognize the revenue up front, which, frankly, is the optimistic reading.
Claire: And the less optimistic one?
Howard: Our finance team's more conservative scenario spreads that revenue over the life of the contract. On that basis, reported growth comes in at around four and a half. Sorry, I should say four to four and a half; there's some currency noise in there too.
Claire: And the acquisition everyone's been writing about?
Howard: It isn't in either number, and I won't comment on speculation.
tasks.question_en: Why could the seven percent headline figure be misleading?
options: It counts all the contract's revenue at once
It already includes the rumored acquisition
It assumes the contract won't close until next year
It's based on the finance team's cautious method
tasks.explanation_ru: Семь процентов предполагают, что контракт закроют в сентябре и выручку признают сразу (recognize the revenue up front) — сам Говард называет это the optimistic reading. Консервативный сценарий финансистов распределяет её по сроку контракта и даёт четыре — четыре с половиной процента, а слухи о покупке компании не входят ни в один прогноз: It isn't in either number.

tasks.script_en:
Monica: Gabriel, your school's been in the news for its phone policy. Some parents call it a ban. Is it?
Gabriel: No, and I'd push back on that word. A flat ban sounds decisive, but honestly, it just turns teachers into phone police, and the kids find workarounds within a week. What we've done is make the default the easy option: phones go into lockers at the start of the day, and that's that.
Monica: And the exceptions?
Gabriel: There are some, of course: kids with medical apps, a few young caregivers. But if a family wants an exception, they sign for it and they take responsibility if it's misused. It's not a free pass, in other words.
Monica: Has it worked?
Gabriel: Early days. Detentions are down, roughly a third. Well, a quarter, if I'm being careful.
tasks.question_en: What is Gabriel's main point about the policy?
options: A total ban, with teachers checking phones all day
Lockers by default, with exceptions families answer for
Free choice for each family, with the school handling misuse
Phones kept in lockers, with no exceptions for anyone
tasks.explanation_ru: Габриэль отвергает слово ban (I'd push back on that word): по умолчанию телефоны уходят в шкафчики — make the default the easy option, — но исключения есть, и семья, которая их просит, должна sign for it and take responsibility. Это не полный запрет с «телефонной полицией», не запрет без исключений и не свобода выбора, где за всё отвечает школа.

tasks.script_en: OK, next question, from a listener whose landlord wants to raise the rent by ten percent. Twelve, actually; I misread that. Here's my advice, and the order really matters. Don't open by asking them to knock it down. The moment you do, the number becomes the only thing you're arguing about. Start instead by reminding them what you're worth as a tenant: you pay on time, you've never called about a blocked sink at midnight. Then put a figure on what losing you would cost them: a month or two empty, cleaning, listing fees. Only once they've acknowledged that, offer to sign for two years instead of one, in exchange for a smaller increase. And the repairs you've been waiting on? Leave those until last, when the money's more or less agreed.
tasks.question_en: When should the listener offer to sign a longer lease?
options: Right at the start, before anything else
After the landlord accepts what losing them would cost
Only once the repairs have been agreed
Before reminding the landlord what a good tenant they are
tasks.explanation_ru: Порядок: не начинать с просьбы о скидке → напомнить, какой вы хороший жилец → оценить, во что владельцу обойдётся потеря жильца → Only once they've acknowledged that, offer to sign for two years → ремонт обсуждать в самом конце (Leave those until last). Длинный договор предлагают только после того, как владелец признал эти издержки.

tasks.script_en:
Sergio: So? How did it go with the board, Alicia? You look, I don't know, half relieved.
Alicia: That's about right. They loved the ambition, or at least they said so. Asked us to tighten up the timeline, which is fine.
Sergio: That sounds good.
Alicia: Wait. They also pushed the funding decision to next quarter and asked for a version that needs half the capital. Half! And the chief risk officer's now sitting in on every review.
Sergio: Did anyone actually say no?
Alicia: Nobody rejected anything outright. But our next slot's been cut from an hour to twenty minutes. No, sorry, to fifteen. I checked the invite this morning.
Sergio: Hmm. Fifteen minutes isn't a presentation; that's a status update.
tasks.question_en: Which detail best shows the board's doubts about the money?
options: They delayed the funding and asked for a half-capital plan
They praised the ambition and asked for a tighter timeline
Nobody on the board rejected the plan outright
The next presentation was cut to fifteen minutes
tasks.explanation_ru: О сомнениях именно в деньгах говорит одно: совет pushed the funding decision to next quarter и попросил вариант, который needs half the capital. Похвала ambition и просьба ужать timeline — знаки интереса, то, что никто не сказал «нет», тоже не о деньгах, а слот, урезанный до пятнадцати минут (No, sorry, to fifteen), говорит об охлаждении к проекту вообще, а не о бюджете.

tasks.script_en: Look, I'll say this up front: duplication's a real problem. We've got three teams, four if you count the contractors, building basically the same reporting tool, so I get why leadership wants to consolidate. But look at the actual chart. Every decision that used to sit with team leads now goes up a level, sometimes two, while our delivery targets haven't moved an inch. And the consultation period? It opens after the new roles have already been announced. So what exactly are we being consulted on? Calling that empowerment is, I think, stretching the word past breaking point. I'm not against merging teams. Honestly, I'd back it tomorrow if the authority moved down, closer to the people who actually carry the risk when something ships late.
tasks.question_en: What is the speaker's attitude toward the reorganization?
options: Accepts the aim, but objects to decisions moving upward
Welcomes the new roles, but wishes consultation had started earlier
Doubts that duplication exists, but likes the new chart
Accepts the new chart, but wants lower delivery targets
tasks.explanation_ru: Цель убрать дублирование говорящий признаёт (duplication's a real problem), но критикует то, что решения уходят наверх (goes up a level, sometimes two), тогда как цели по срокам не изменились. Слияние он поддержит, if the authority moved down, closer to the people who actually carry the risk. Позднюю консультацию он приводит как ещё один симптом, а новые роли и схему не одобряет.

tasks.script_en: And finally, a story that's been, shall we say, a little overhyped. You may have seen headlines claiming that a daily walk cuts your risk of dementia in half. The study behind them is real, and fairly large: about twelve thousand adults, well, twelve and a half thousand, followed for nine years. But what it actually found is that people who walked roughly forty minutes a day had a risk about a third lower than those who barely walked at all. Not half. A third. And that's an association, not proof of cause, since people in the early stages of decline may simply walk less. The authors themselves are careful on this point; it's the press releases that weren't. None of which, of course, is a reason to stay on the couch.
tasks.question_en: According to the study, how much lower was the risk for people who walked about forty minutes a day?
options: About half
About a third
About forty percent
About twelve percent
tasks.explanation_ru: Заголовки обещали in half, но ведущий уточняет: a risk about a third lower... Not half. A third. Forty — это минуты ходьбы в день, а twelve — тысячи участников исследования.

tasks.script_en:
Julia: Marco, your city's introduced a daily fee for day-trippers. Critics are calling it a tax on curiosity. Is that fair?
Marco: It's a good line, I'll give them that. But the fee isn't really about revenue; it barely covers the cost of collecting it. The point is to spread visitors out. On a peak Saturday we get, what, eighty thousand people, some days closer to ninety, in a historic center built for maybe a tenth of that.
Julia: So you're pricing people out.
Marco: We're pricing people into Tuesday. The fee only applies on about thirty peak days, and it's waived for anyone staying overnight, because those visitors actually sustain local businesses rather than just, you know, passing through.
Julia: And if it doesn't work?
Marco: Then we've learned something cheaply, and we'll drop it.
tasks.question_en: What is Marco's main argument?
options: The fee mainly raises money to protect the historic center
The fee is meant to spread visits out, not to raise money
The fee is meant to keep day-trippers away from the city
The fee should also apply to visitors who stay overnight
tasks.explanation_ru: Марко прямо отделяет сбор от дохода (isn't really about revenue) и называет цель: to spread visitors out — We're pricing people into Tuesday, то есть переносит поездки на спокойные дни. Отпугивать туристов вообще он не хочет, а для тех, кто ночует в городе, сбор отменён (waived).

tasks.script_en: Hi, it's Deborah from Lane Realty, following up on the sale. So, the buyers' lender has, finally, signed off on the appraisal, which means we can move forward, but the order really matters here. Before anything gets scheduled, I need the signed disclosure form back; I can't release the draft contract without it. Once the buyers have reviewed that draft, their inspector wants one more visit. The whole house again, no, sorry, just the roof. Assuming nothing new turns up, we'll book the closing, and you hand over the keys at the closing itself, not before, whatever their agent suggests. Oh, and please don't cancel your home insurance until the funds have actually cleared. Call me if any of that's unclear.
tasks.question_en: What must happen immediately before the roof inspection?
options: The seller returns the signed disclosure form
The buyers review the draft contract
The seller hands over the keys
The closing date is booked
tasks.explanation_ru: Цепочка такая: подписанная disclosure form → черновик договора → Once the buyers have reviewed that draft, their inspector wants one more visit → closing и передача ключей прямо на нём. Непосредственно перед осмотром крыши покупатели изучают черновик; форма нужна раньше, а closing и ключи — позже.

tasks.script_en:
Kevin: Coach, you took Marcus Sanchez off at halftime. Is he injured?
Diane: No, he's fine. Fully fit.
Kevin: Then why bench him in a game you needed to win?
Diane: Look, we have to think beyond tonight. The young guys need minutes, and, frankly, they need to learn to win without leaning on one player.
Kevin: There've been reports of offers from Europe. Any truth to that?
Diane: I'm not going to comment on rumors. What I will say is that Marcus has given this club seven great years, eight, actually, if you count the youth team, and whatever happens this summer, people here will remember that.
Kevin: That sounds a lot like a goodbye.
Diane: It's a thank-you. Next question.
tasks.question_en: What do the coach's answers suggest?
options: Sanchez is hiding an injury from the press
Sanchez will leave the club soon
The coach is unhappy with how Sanchez played
The young players will be sold this summer
tasks.explanation_ru: Прямо тренер ничего не подтверждает, но подводит итог годам Маркуса в клубе (has given this club seven great years), добавляет whatever happens this summer и заранее учит молодых выигрывать without leaning on one player — всё это похоже на подготовку к его уходу. Травму она отрицает (Fully fit), а претензий к его игре не высказывает.

tasks.script_en: I'll admit I went in expecting to hate it. A three-hour documentary about, of all things, a public library sounded like a punishment. And the first hour does test your patience: no narration, no music, just meetings about budgets. But somewhere in the second hour, I realized I'd stopped checking the time. Watching a librarian spend twenty minutes helping an elderly man fill out a benefits form is more moving than most thrillers manage. Is it too long? Probably, yes, by about forty minutes, maybe even an hour. Would I sit through it again? Honestly, I'm not sure I would. But I'm glad I saw it once, and I've been recommending it to, well, my more patient friends.
tasks.question_en: What is the speaker's overall attitude toward the documentary?
options: Moved by the second hour, but wouldn't recommend it to anyone
Glad to have seen it, though unsure about watching it again
Found it too long, but keen to watch it again soon
Enjoyed the first hour, but found the second one too slow
tasks.explanation_ru: Говорящий шёл с мыслью, что фильм ему не понравится (expecting to hate it), и признаёт, что он too long, но со второго часа перестал смотреть на часы и рад, что посмотрел: I'm glad I saw it once. Пересматривать он не уверен (I'm not sure I would), хотя советует фильм my more patient friends. Первый час, наоборот, испытывает терпение, а тронул его второй.
